text:
Rowan: Heads-up  UX check for thresholds + preview. Two quick questions: 1) should units live in an inline micro-dropdown or a compact toggle labelled 'short/long'? 2) suppression preview currently hides fallback channels and overlaps the rule label at narrow widths. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/ux/preview-overlap-2.png

Priya: I'm leaning to the micro-dropdown for clarity, but make it keyboard-friendly (arrow keys to open, esc to close). For the compact view, show `5m` visually and expose the verbose form via aria-describedby.

Ethan: Accessibility note: ensure the numeric input supports spin controls and accept `aria-valuemin/max/step` so ATs can manipulate values without toggling separate controls. Also avoid placeholder-only labels.

Sofia: Mobile pattern proposal: progressive disclosure  show first pill row + "+N more". When expanded, use a stacked list with clear group header "Previewing channels" and role=group + aria-roledescription='channels list' so SRs announce context. Avoid horizontal scroll.

Priya: Copy nit: current helper says "when error rate > 2%". Suggest: "when error rate exceeds 2% (p90, over 5 min)" or configurable percentile tag. Also suggest a small info icon that opens a tooltip explaining p90 vs p95.

Ethan: For suppressed channels, don't remove them from DOM when muted  visually dim and add aria-hidden=false plus aria-label like "Channel X muted" so ATs know state. Use aria-live polite region to announce toggles: "Suppression enabled  2 channels muted".

a11y-bot: Contrast scan: muted pill text #6B6B6B on #FFFFFF = 3.9 ratio. Recommendation: token color neutral-700 (#333333) or increase font-weight to 600 at 14px to hit 4.5. Also recommend focus-visible outline of 3px for pills when keyboard focused.

Rowan: UX thought: surface fallback routing in preview with a subtle divider: "Primary: Slack (low latency)  Fallback: Email (on error)". Also show a small latency badge on primaries that use latency routing.

Sofia: Edge case: when a rule is templated (uses variables) preview should show resolved example values, and an inline link to toggle between "example" and "raw template" views. This helps users confirm thresholds.

Priya: Keyboard flow acceptance: threshold input -> unit dropdown -> spin controls -> suppression toggle -> preview expand -> save. No focus traps in preview expand. Also add a `Shift+Tab` visible focus order check in tests.

Ethan: Implementation note: expose aria-controls from the toggle to the preview list id, and set aria-expanded on the +N control. That helps SRs announce expansion. Also log telemetry when users expand preview so we can measure confusion hotspots.

Rowan-bot: Added Figma frame comments: https://figma.redwood.in/frame/alerting-thresholds-v4. Action items: Priya to update helper copy & tooltip content, Ethan to add aria attributes and numeric spin support spec, Sofia to mock mobile stacked preview + roledescription, Rowan to pick accessible color token and update the pill states. Target: next design check Thursday.

Priya: Will post copy options by tomorrow EOD.

Sofia: I'll upload mobile mock and interaction notes by Wednesday.

Ethan: I'll sketch aria attributes and a11y test checklist.

Rowan: thanks team, let's try to include a quick accessibility smoke test in the dev handoff checklist :eyes:
